quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You see a green light ahead, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Enter the intersection partway to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter the intersection unless you can drive completely across it.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection unless you can drive completely across it.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you cannot enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane. What should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must let you go first.
You must let the pedestrian go first.
Honk your horn to warn them you are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let the pedestrian go first.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind people use a white cane or guide dog. You must give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A yield sign is ahead.
A road is entering from the left.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yield sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. How can you prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive slower.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Slow down in rain to avoid hydroplaning. Driving too fast can cause your tires to ride on water and lose grip on the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: When can you drive on the shoulder to pass another car?

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder.

questions.question: How should you enter an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, look for cars, and enter when safe.
Look for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and smoothly merge with fast-moving traffic. Do not stop as you would on regular roads.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your speed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what will likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
Traffic will move better.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you block traffic by driving too slowly, you may get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going over the speed limit.

questions.question: Before you stop at a traffic light or sign, what should you do first?

options.text: Press the accelerator hard.
Check your mirrors for other cars.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for other cars.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see surrounding traffic. Be aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then move your foot to the brake and press firmly for a smooth stop.

questions.question: After you pass a vehicle moving in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, do not return to your original lane until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back into your original lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where animals, people, and vehicles are likely to cross the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn drivers of situations that might not be obvious. This sign warns you about an upcoming intersection so you can prepare for traffic or turning.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Driving as close to the right edge of the road as possible and stopping.
Moving into the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving as close to the right edge of the road as possible and stopping.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check that no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic beside and behind your vehicle before changing lanes.

questions.question: As your speed increases, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look well ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop as your speed increases. When driving fast, look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead winds with turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you to be careful when the road is wet, as the pavement becomes slippery and harder to navigate safely.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It may frustrate drivers behind you and cause them to make unsafe moves to pass you. Drive with traffic flow, within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving because you cannot see as well. It is harder to judge speed and distance. Increase your following distance to prevent a collision if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. Use your headlights properly, following the rules for high and low beams.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always be very careful when backing up.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which of these is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not paying attention to workers and moving equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is coming, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop.
Honk to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. When you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of freeway traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.
